components.role: Candidate answer-marker and numerical-information processing component. Its identity change mainly reweights shared read/write associations and has comparatively strong update-to-feature correspondence. Actual routing and normalized contribution remain unknown.

Candidate reduced numerical suppression: A weakens an anti-copy-aligned OV coefficient through within-subspace reweighting and write-direction rotation, mainly associated with O-projection changes. Whole-block normalization may modify its effective contribution.

Numerical-value reuse candidate with a strongly copy-aligned OV map, A-favoring identity coefficients across tested numeral families, and some near-source matching-kernel changes. The selected information and actual attention are unknown.

Candidate numerical reinforcement pathway with A-favoring identity changes across multiple representations. Both within-span reweighting and write-direction rotation contribute; no copying behavior was observed.

A weakens an anti-copy-aligned numerical OV coefficient through mixed readout reweighting and substantial write-subspace rotation. This is not a simple gain change, and correspondence-specificity evidence is limited.

Candidate competing numerical pathway: up-path and gate-path identity coefficient changes have opposing signs across several representations. Contextual unit signs and post-MLP normalization prevent determining the net effect.

Distributed numerical write-weight changes, especially in down projections, with illustrative units 750, 824, 1242, and 1464. These are numerical weight associations, not unconditional number-promoting units; gating and normalized contributions remain contextual.

Changed operator and answer-marker associations. Query-read subspace rotation contributes substantially to its number-query/minus-versus-times coefficient change. Normalized routing, arithmetic computation, and correctness were not verified.

Positional-selection candidate: a copy-aligned OV map accompanies more near-favoring numerical-matching kernel changes in A. This is a weight-kernel property; nearby information is not known to be a user guess.
Opposing positional-selection candidate: A decreases near-versus-far numerical-matching shape coefficients in a copy-aligned head. No actual attention preference or truthfulness role was established.

evidence: Weak subjective identification, not behavioral verification. Thirty-two weight-only runs found numerical identity changes, anti-copy weakening, answer/operator-associated coefficients, and mixed positional-kernel changes. Several survive geometric and reparameterization controls, but exact-inactivity controls demonstrate that prominent naive signatures can be nonfunctional. No MLP unit received an input-independent polarity certificate. Q/K and output-normalization bounds show that coefficient changes cannot generally be interpreted as normalized contribution changes without contextual states. No forward passes or activations were used. Components are ranked investigation candidates, not a verified causal importance ranking.
